$comment: Forbidden-claim catalogue for the built site (AAASM-5696). Checked by scripts/check-forbidden-claims.py against build/ output, NOT source. Canonical authority is ADR 0033 in ai-agent-assembly/agent-assembly (docs/src/adr/0033-canonical-governance-and-enforcement-architecture.md) -- its 'Explicitly forbidden designs' section and the section 6 claim vocabulary. Do not restate the ADR here; add phrases and cite the design they violate.

$rules.framing_not_sentences: Entries MUST be the bare FRAMING, never a full sentence copied from one page. The first version of this catalogue held '/product's whole sentence, so it matched that one page and missed the same framing on the blog, which continues '...layers: SDK (in-process)'. A sentence-shaped entry finds an instance; a framing-shaped entry finds the class. This is the single most important rule in this file.
$rules.prose_only: Single common words (universal, complete, comprehensive) are marked prose_only. They are searched in reader-facing text only, never in JS bundles, where 'autocomplete' and React internals produce pure noise -- 22 false positives when this was measured.
$rules.word_boundary: prose_only entries are matched on WORD BOUNDARIES, because a bare substring 'complete' also matches 'incomplete', which asserts the opposite. Boundaries are applied via Python re (\b), never via grep -E, which accepts \b and silently ignores it.
$rules.positive_control: Every phrase is proven matchable against a synthetic fixture before any absence is reported. An absence with no positive control is not a measurement.
$rules.additive_only: This file may EXTEND the gate, never narrow it. The 14 ADR 0033 fd-7 absolutes are not here: they are FD7_ABSOLUTES in check-forbidden-claims.py, because they are never waivable (ADR 0034 Decision 10) and deleting a line from a data file does not look like disabling a check, whereas deleting a line from the script does. An fd-7 group added back here is ignored and reported as an integrity failure. AAASM-5730.

phrases.why: The fixed SDK -> proxy -> eBPF pipeline as THE architecture, in prose or as a three-box diagram. The any_units entries carry a {unit} slot expanded over layer/tier/level/stage/plane in check-forbidden-claims.py, because the framing is what is forbidden and the noun carrying it is interchangeable: five reworded instances escaped the literal list by substituting exactly this word. 'kernel layer' stays literal on purpose -- 'at the kernel level' is ordinary technical prose, not a claim.

phrases.why: eBPF (or 'the kernel layer') as a cross-platform or universal final layer, or as a mechanism that catches everything including bypass attempts. The any_units entries cover the 'each one catches what the previous one missed' shape, whose noun is likewise interchangeable.
The gateway as a fourth interception layer. It is E1 and holds no traffic.

The hero framing AAASM-5585 removed from the homepage: the product described as a governance layer for agents. 'governance {unit} for' replaces the three literal 'governance layer for ...' entries -- it covers them plus the noun the rewording used ('the governance plane for autonomous software') and does not depend on guessing what follows 'for'.
Approval claims must use the ADR 0033 section 6 term 'Approval required' and carry their bound. No shipped operator surface answers the queue (AAASM-5657), so a hold times out into a refusal.

Not on the ADR's literal list, so NOT an fd-7 violation and not treated as one. These are the same claim shape reached by synonym, found on the blog during AAASM-5696. Recorded here so the class is visible; if the owners want them binding, they belong in the ADR's list first, not in this file.
